sources.//: This `exclude` list is the template engine's own default list MINUS `**/*.lock.json`, and it exists to keep that one pattern off (FS.GG.Templates#384, same root cause as #380). The default is not inert: it silently stripped both committed `packages.lock.json` files out of every generated workspace, so the reviewed locks could never reach a product. Combined with `Directory.Build.props`'s `RestorePackagesWithLockFile=true`, the product's FIRST restore then AUTHORED its own lock from whatever the ambient host happened to resolve, and `RestoreLockedMode=true` enforced that unreviewed lock forever after — surfacing as `NU1403: Package content hash validation failed` the moment the ambient content moved. `tests/composition/fable-bindings/run.sh` passed throughout, because a restore that authors its own lock cannot disagree with it; the defect was latent, not absent. Declaring `exclude` here REPLACES the engine default wholesale, so every other default pattern below must be restated verbatim; they are copied from the engine's own defaults, read out of dotnet SDK 10.0.302's Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Orchestrator.RunnableProjects.dll (`strings -el` emits `**/*` as the include, then these six plus `**/*.lock.json` as the exclude). `**/node_modules/**` is restated deliberately: this template IS an npm workspace, and a maintainer who has run `npm install` in it would otherwise ship their entire installed dependency tree into every generated product.

productName.description: Binding/library name; --name is used when omitted.

npmPackage.description: The selected v1 declaration corpus; arbitrary packages require a separately qualified template.

bindingTarget.description: Selected corpus has real-browser evidence; node remains an additional smoke lane.

symbols.//effectiveNameLower: Required by FS.GG.Templates#384, and only once the lockfiles actually reach a product. NuGet writes a ProjectReference into `packages.lock.json` under the referenced project's LOWERCASED name — `tests/BindingsProduct.CompileTests/packages.lock.json` carries a `"bindingsproduct"` entry. `effectiveName` above renames the project to the product's name but does not touch that lowercase spelling, so a delivered lock would name a project the generated workspace does not contain and `--locked-mode` would refuse the restore with NU1004 (`The packages lock file is inconsistent with the project dependencies`). This symbol is what keeps the delivered lock describing the delivered projects. `fs-gg-console` has carried the same symbol for the same lowercase reason since before this item.
